chunks: From Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

While my father was seated and in his presence were a number of people, he suddenly laughed until his eyes filled with tears. Then he said: 'Do you know what made me laugh?' They said, 'No.' He said: 'Ibn Abbas claims that he is among those who said: Our Lord is Allah, then stood firm [41:30]. So I said to him: Have you ever seen the Angels, O Ibn Abbas, informing you of their guardianship over you in this world and the next, along with security from fear and grief?

He said: Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: 'The believers are but brothers' [49:10], and the entire community is included in this. So I smiled and said: You speak the truth, O Ibn Abbas! I adjure you by Allah — is there any contradiction in the rulings of Allah, Majestic is His Mention? He said: No.

So I said: What is your view regarding a man who struck another man's fingers with a sword until they fell off, then he left, and another man came and severed his palm, and the case is brought to you while you are a judge — how would you rule? He said: I would tell this cutter to give him the blood money for his palm, and I would tell the one whose hand was cut to reach a settlement on whatever terms he wishes and to send him to people of justice.

I said: Then contradiction has entered the rulings of Allah, Mighty is His Mention, and you have contradicted your first words. Allah, Mighty is His Mention, refuses to establish anything among His creation from the legal penalties without its interpretation existing on earth. Cut off the hand of the palm-cutter from its root, then give him the blood money for the fingers. Such is the ruling of Allah on the night in which His command descends. If you were to deny it after what you heard from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), then Allah would admit you into the Fire just as He blinded your sight on the day you denied it against Ali ibn Abi Talib.

He said: Was it for that reason my sight was blinded? And what made you know that? By Allah, my sight was not blinded except by the stroke of an angel's wing. He said: So I smiled and left him that day due to the feebleness of his intellect.

Then I met him and said: O Ibn Abbas! You did not speak with truthfulness as you did yesterday. Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) told you: The Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr) is in every year, and the command of the year descends on that night, and for that command there are guardians after the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). So you asked: Who are they? He said: I and eleven from my descendants — Imams who are spoken to (Muhaddathun).

So you said: I do not see it as having been except with the Messenger of Allah. Then the angel who used to speak to him appeared to you and said: You lie, O Abdullah! My eyes saw what Ali narrated to you, and his eyes did not see him, but his heart preserved it and it settled in his hearing, then he struck you with his wing and you were blinded. He said: Then Ibn Abbas said: Whatever we disagree about, its judgment is with Allah. So I said to him: Did Allah ever rule with two commands in a single matter? He said: No. So I said: Here is where you have perished and caused others to perish.

key_terms.الَّذِينَ قَالُوا رَبُّنَا اللَّهُ ثُمَّ: Those who say 'Our Lord is Allah, then stand firm' — Quran 41:30, referring to those promised angelic guardianship
key_terms.دِيَة: Diya — blood money, financial compensation for bodily harm under Islamic law
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ: Laylat al-Qadr — the Night of Decree/Power, when divine commands for the year descend
key_terms.مُحَدَّثُونَ: Muhaddathun — those spoken to by angels; a special rank of the Imams below prophethood
key_terms.وَلَايَة: Wilayah — guardianship, authority, protection; here referring to the angelic guardianship promised to the truly steadfast
key_terms.وُلَاة: Wulat — guardians, those entrusted with divine authority after the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about Ibn Abbas and Laylat al-Qadr?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates an account from his father (Imam al-Baqir AS) in which Ibn Abbas was challenged on his claim to be among the 'steadfast believers' of Quran 41:30. The Imam exposed the contradiction in Ibn Abbas's understanding of divine law through a case study on blood money (diya), then revealed that Ibn Abbas's blindness was caused by an angel's wing-strike when he denied Imam Ali's (AS) knowledge of Laylat al-Qadr. The hadith establishes the doctrine that the Imams are Muhaddathun (spoken to by angels) and that there is no contradiction in divine rulings — only one valid interpretation exists on earth, held by the Imam of each age.
